# ethereum-optimism/optimism Weekly Report (Jul 12 - 18, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, the Optimism ecosystem made significant strides in decoupling core infrastructure from `op-geth` while advancing the performance and security of the Kona fault proof stack. A major focus was placed on the transition to a Rust-based script engine for deployments and the resolution of critical unauthenticated attack surfaces in Kona. Additionally, the team streamlined the developer experience by enhancing observability metrics for hardforks and refining node operator documentation to address pruning and synchronization requirements.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Infrastructure & `op-geth` Decoupling
A primary theme this week was the strategic effort to reduce dependencies on `op-geth` and streamline the monorepo.
*   **CI & Feature Cleanup:** Removed `op-geth` CI variants and the `CANNON_KONA` development feature toggle to simplify the codebase following the U19 contracts audit ([#21715](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21715), [#21663](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21663)).
*   **Script Engine Transition:** Initiated the replacement of the Go-based script engine with a Rust/revm-based `op-script-engine` for `op-deployer`, including support for forked script hosts ([#21750](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21750), [#21752](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21752)).
*   **Deployment Tooling:** Enhanced `op-deployer` to predict L1 proxy addresses during the `prepare` command, solving a critical hurdle in L2 genesis generation ([#21560](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21560)).

### Kona & Fault Proof Enhancements
Significant work was dedicated to hardening and optimizing the Kona stack.
*   **Security Fixes:** Addressed three unauthenticated attack surfaces in Kona to improve protocol robustness ([#21713](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21713), [#21753](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21753)).
*   **Performance:** Optimized the `kona-driver` by decoding only L1-info deposits when computing `L2BlockInfo`, reducing unnecessary overhead ([#21737](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21737)).
*   **Dispute Game Logic:** Updated `op-challenger` to use the selected VM for state conversion, ensuring proper Cannon-Kona registration ([#21739](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21739)).

### Observability & Node Operations
Improvements were made to how operators monitor and run OP Stack nodes.
*   **Metrics:** Introduced Prometheus metrics for `op-reth` and `op-node` to track chain hardfork activation schedules ([#21704](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21704)).
*   **Node Guidance:** Updated documentation to clarify that `--minimal` pruning is not supported for OP Stack nodes, preventing common synchronization failures ([#21672](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21672)).
*   **RPC Parity:** Implemented DA throttling RPC methods (`eth_setDAGasPrice`) in `op-reth` to maintain parity with `op-geth` ([#13063](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/13063)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Soundness Reviews:** Successfully closed the review of Kona host game input and witness generation ([#18430](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18430)).
*   **Challenger Requirements:** Fixed a bug where `op-challenger` incorrectly required a local `cannon-prestate` despite having a `--prestate-url` configured ([#21470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21470)).
*   **Build Reliability:** Resolved intermittent "Text file busy" flakes in Docker builds by serializing `solc` installations ([#21734](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21734)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Kona SP1 Performance:** A new concern was raised regarding the performance of EIP-2537 precompiles in `kona-sp1` due to the lack of hardware acceleration for `arkworks` ([#21767](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21767)).
*   **Dispute Game Interface:** Ongoing discussion regarding adding `closeGame()` to the `IDisputeGame` interface to simplify how `op-challenger` handles the `AnchorStateRegistry` for finalized games ([#21678](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21678)).
*   **DevOps Ergonomics:** A proposal is under review to ensure all `op-reth` command-line options are configurable via environment variables ([#21719](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21719)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week saw active coordination between the protocol and tooling teams, particularly regarding the `op-geth` decoupling strategy. There was significant collaborative effort in refining the `op-script-engine` transition, involving multiple spikes and parity checks. The community also focused on improving the contributor experience by introducing version-controlled git hooks and clearer PR description guidelines to manage the high volume of incoming changes.
